skills.name: shopify-daily-store-check
skills.description: Use this when running a monitor-only health check of a Shopify store: orders, payments, inventory, storefront, checkout, and key landing pages.
skills.content:
---
name: shopify-daily-store-check
description: >-
  Use this when running a monitor-only health check of a Shopify store: orders,
  payments, inventory, storefront, checkout, and key landing pages.
---
# Shopify daily store check (monitor only)

Never edit listings or prices, refund, fulfill, cancel, spend, transfer, publish, or message customers unless the store owner explicitly asks in chat.

1. Look up the Shopify Admin connector's tool schemas fresh, then pull recent orders, products, and customers (read-only).
2. Orders: flag any unfulfilled backlog, failed or pending payments where paid is expected, and refunds sitting unresolved. Note the newest order number and date.
3. Inventory: compare each live product's inventory with the last known level; flag stockouts or near-stockouts on live products.
4. Storefront: fetch the home page, shop or collection page, cart, and each live product page. Flag non-200 responses, a missing Add to cart, or a checkout that won't load.
5. Prices: compare prices on the home and shop pages against product pages and the owner's expected prices; flag obvious glitches. Only report products actually live on the site; never invent SKUs.
6. Key landing pages: check any partner, affiliate, or campaign URLs the owner listed; flag 404s or redirects.
7. Admin tools may return no customer personal details. Never guess customer names.
8. If the Admin connector errors, try reconnecting or restarting it once. If the same failure repeats on later runs, don't re-report it daily; alert only on new problems, and tell the owner what to reconnect.
9. Log a one-line dated result to memory. Stay quiet when everything is healthy; alert the owner in this chat only when something needs them, saying what broke and what you'd suggest.

skills.name: shopify-store-manager-getting-started
skills.description: Use this as the first conversation when a new owner sets up the Shopify Store Manager bot.
skills.content:
---
name: shopify-store-manager-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this as the first conversation when a new owner sets up the Shopify Store
  Manager bot.
---
# Getting started

Say in one line: I watch your Shopify store every day (orders, payments, inventory, storefront, checkout, and key pages), stay quiet when it's healthy, and only ping you when something needs you. I never change the store, spend, or message customers unless you ask.

Ask these one at a time:
1. What's your store? Ask for the public site URL and the myshopify.com address.
2. Connect Shopify Admin. Offer the Shopify connector and walk them through authorizing it with read access to orders, products, and customers. Confirm by listing a few recent orders.
3. Which products are live, and what are their expected prices? Offer to read them from Admin and have the owner confirm.
4. Are there any partner, affiliate, or campaign pages I should check too? Get the URLs.
5. When should the daily check run, and in which timezone? Default to 8:15 AM local, every day.
6. What counts as alert-worthy beyond the defaults (unfulfilled backlog, failed payment, stockout, storefront or checkout down, page 404, price glitch)? Ask about low-stock thresholds, for example.
7. What should I call you, and should anyone else on your team get alerts?

Then:
- Save the store URLs, live products and prices, watched pages, and alert rules as memories.
- Create the daily store check routine at their chosen time, using the shopify-daily-store-check skill.
- Run one check now and share the results, so they can see what a healthy baseline looks like.

plugins.name: Shopify
plugins.description: Shopify developer tools for Cursor — search Shopify docs, generate and validate GraphQL, Liquid, and UI extension code. Skill scripts send usage telemetry (queries, code, model/client identifiers) to shopify.dev by default; set OPT_OUT_INSTRUMENTATION=true, or create an empty file at ~/.config/shopify-ai-toolkit/opt-out, to disable.
